syllabus_topics: Introduction and review of basic concepts: review of internal organization and operation of a computer; perspective on recent and future evolution.

Computer organization: CISC vs RISC processors; constraints of technological evolution of computers; code generation, role of compilers; data organization in memory; number representation, IEEE 754 format; performance metrics.
Operation of a RISC processor: organization; pipeline processing; data, control, and structural pipeline conflicts; code optimization.

Memory system: memory hierarchy; primary memory; cache memory architecture; program optimization; memory management, connection to the operating system; efficient address translation mechanisms; integrated operation of the memory system.
Input/output system: analog-digital interface; performance in communication with peripherals; characteristics of standard buses; peripheral interface.
assessment_rules: The final grade N is calculated as: N = 60% × max{ [50% × max(MAP45_1, Ex_1) + 50% × max(MAP45_2, Ex_2)], EE } + 40% × L, where L is the individual laboratory component grade. Minimum grade for the average of the two MAPs (or corresponding exam parts) is 8 values. The minimum grade for the laboratory component (L) is 9 values. There is no evaluation during the resit period.
